company_name: C&D International Investment Group Limited (建發國際投資集團)
overview: C&D International is a Xiamen-based, state-backed Chinese residential property developer, majority-owned through C&D Inc. (廈門建發股份, a Fujian state-owned conglomerate) via an intermediate holding company. The Group develops and sells residential and mixed-use property across roughly 50 Chinese cities, with revenue concentrated in tier-1/tier-2 hubs (Hangzhou, Shanghai, Beijing, Xiamen, Suzhou), and also earns a small, growing stream from property management and construction-management subsidiaries. Note: not to be confused with China Overseas Property Holdings (2669.HK), a separate property-management-only company.

business_model.summary: Primarily a build-and-sell residential developer: land is acquired, projects are developed and pre-sold, and revenue is recognised on handover (completion), so reported revenue lags contracted sales by roughly 1-2 years. A smaller 'second curve' of recurring/fee income comes from two listed subsidiaries - C&D Property Management (HK.02156) and C&D Holsin engineering consulting (SH.603909) - plus investment properties. FY2025 property development was 96.8% of revenue; property management and other related services (property management, construction management, entrusted construction) was 3.2%.

revenue_streams.name: Property management & other related services (C&D Property, C&D Holsin, entrusted construction)

business_model.customer_type: B2C (residential home buyers), with some B2B/government land-acquisition and construction-management relationships
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Mainland China; FY2025 sales concentrated in Hangzhou, Suzhou, Shanghai, Xiamen, Beijing, Quanzhou and other Fujian/Yangtze-Delta cities, with expansion into Beijing/Shanghai/Hangzhou/Chengdu 'core cities' in FY2025 land acquisition

main_competitors: C&D Real Estate Group (sister SOE developer)
competitive_position.market_position: Mid-to-large-cap state-affiliated developer; one of the few developers to grow or hold share through the downturn via its state-owned funding advantage, ranked among the larger contracted-sales developers nationally (~RMB122bn total contracted sales FY2025) as many private peers have defaulted or shrunk sharply.

moat_factors.description: Loans from intermediate holding company (C&D Inc. group) of ~RMB38.9bn at FY2025-end at 4.06% give access to funding at rates and tenors private developers cannot match, a critical advantage as banks and bond markets discriminate against non-SOE developers.

moat_factors.factor: Low cost of capital / financing cost trend
moat_factors.description: Blended borrowing cost fell further in 2026 (reported ~3.15%), among the lowest in the sector, aided by SOE status and improving balance sheet.

Premium product positioning in core cities (Xiamen, Beijing, Shanghai, Chengdu) with flagship projects outselling local comps, but brand power is regional/national rather than a hard moat versus COLI, Vanke, or Greentown.
~83% of land reserve value was acquired after 2022 (i.e., post-downturn, lower-cost, higher-margin land), reducing legacy impairment risk versus older-vintage peers.

weaknesses: No network effects, switching costs, or regulatory barrier moat - property development is fundamentally commoditized and cyclical
High reliance on parent-company and bank debt funding (gearing ratio 87.5% of total borrowings/equity at FY2025-end)

Contracted sales and attributable sales both declining double digits YoY (FY2025 attributable sales -12.0%; H1 2026 attributable sales -8.4%), signalling continued volume/share pressure even relative to a shrinking market
Thin and declining net margins (down from ~6.6% in FY2021 to ~2.7% in FY2025) show weak pricing power and rising selling-expense intensity in a buyer's market
Minority-interest heavy project structure (large NCI balance ~RMB54bn) dilutes value for Company shareholders and complicates read-through from headline Group revenue to attributable profit

growth_drivers: Industry consolidation: private developers' defaults and capital constraints are shifting market share toward well-funded SOE/state-affiliated developers like C&D International
'Flagship project' (燈塔) product strategy driving premium pricing and faster sell-through versus local competing projects in core cities
Selective, high-conviction land acquisition in core cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Hangzhou, Chengdu, Fujian) - FY2025 added 41 projects for ~RMB65.4bn, implying ~RMB130.4bn of future saleable value
Continued reduction in financing costs (reported ~3.15% blended rate in 2026) as an SOE-advantaged lower-cost developer, supporting margin vs. peers

'Second curve' diversification into property management (C&D Property, HK.02156) and construction/engineering management (C&D Holsin, SH.603909), both growing revenue double digits and providing a partial offset to the core development decline
'Good houses' (好房子) national policy push toward higher-quality, differentiated housing, which plays to C&D's premium flagship-project positioning
Government policy support for project completions, urban renewal, and destocking that benefits well-capitalized developers able to execute

business.description: Full-scope contracted sales fell ~8.6% in FY2025 to RMB122bn and attributable sales fell ~12.0%; H1 2026 attributable contracted sales fell a further ~8.4% YoY, indicating the volume decline has not stabilized.

business.risk: Revenue/earnings decline as pre-sales roll off
business.description: Revenue fell 4.3% in FY2025 and H1 2026 revenue fell ~48% YoY (RMB17.8bn vs ~RMB32.8bn-34.2bn in prior H1s per filings) as the handover pipeline from the weaker 2023-2024 sales cohort flows through; profit attributable to equity holders fell 24% in FY2025 and ~9.7% in H1 2026.

Large and growing non-controlling interests (~RMB54-68bn across FY2024-2025) mean a meaningful share of project-level profit does not accrue to Company shareholders, and project-level JV/NCI structures are opaque.
Company explicitly flags buyer and partner default risk in its key risk factors disclosure, relevant given weak household balance sheets and slower mortgage completion in a downturn.

financial.description: Gearing ratio (total borrowings/total equity) was 87.5% at FY2025-end; ~RMB38.9bn (>50%) of interest-bearing debt was loans from the intermediate holding company (C&D Inc. group) at 4.06%, creating reliance on continued parent willingness/capacity to fund, rather than a diversified, arm's-length capital structure.

Net debt rose to RMB33.5bn (net debt/equity ~34.8%) at FY2025-end from RMB32.6bn a year earlier, despite falling cash balances (RMB50.6bn vs RMB57.3bn); ~RMB13.1bn of borrowings are due within one year.
RMB19.05bn of guarantees outstanding at FY2025-end (down from RMB43.3bn) for buyer mortgage financing - a contingent liability common to the sector that could crystallize in a deeper downturn.

Scrip-dividend option (final dividend HK$0.9/share, FY2025) suggests the company is managing cash conservation even while maintaining shareholder returns; sustained payouts amid falling attributable profit could pressure the balance sheet if not funded from genuine FCF.

regulatory.description: Although enforcement has loosened, Chinese regulators retain broad authority over developer leverage, pre-sale fund escrow, and project completion obligations; policy reversals could tighten financing conditions again.

regulatory.risk: Land appreciation tax and local government land policy
regulatory.description: PRC land appreciation tax is a direct lever on profitability (tax expense fell YoY in FY2025 partly due to lower LAT), and local-government land auction/relief policy changes affect land cost and margin.

Heavy reliance on intermediate holding company loans invites scrutiny of related-party terms and could be constrained by future SOE-sector deleveraging directives from Beijing or Fujian provincial authorities.

macro.description: Fitch and S&P project further declines in national new-home sales value in 2026 (Fitch: -7-8% to below RMB7 trillion); no analyst consensus yet sees a clear market bottom, directly pressuring C&D's core volumes and prices.
Company's own chairman's statement cites weak willingness of residents to invest/consume in home purchases as the central 2025 challenge, a condition largely outside the company's control.

macro.risk: Interest rate and credit cycle sensitivity
macro.description: ~93% of Group borrowings are floating rate, so PBOC rate policy directly affects financing costs; conversely, further PBOC easing would be a tailwind for both company funding costs and buyer mortgage affordability.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese residential new-home sales are forecast to keep declining in 2026 (Fitch: -7-8% in value; S&P had seen -6% in primary sales), with no consensus bottom yet. However, ~75% of Fitch-rated Chinese homebuilders are now SOEs, and the share of issuers on negative outlook/watch has fallen sharply (from ~60% at end-2024 to ~25%), reflecting improving credit metrics concentrated among leading SOEs - the cohort C&D International sits in.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - residential property development is one of the most cyclical sectors, driven by household income/confidence, mortgage rates, and local government land/housing policy; C&D's volumes have fallen for multiple consecutive periods alongside the broader market.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - ~93% of borrowings are floating rate; lower PBOC rates reduce financing costs and improve buyer affordability, a double tailwind, while rate increases work in reverse.
key_input_costs: Financing/borrowing costs (incl. parent company loan rates)
PRC land appreciation tax and other transaction taxes

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 revenue fell ~48% YoY to RMB17.8bn and net profit attributable to equity holders fell ~9.7% YoY to RMB825m, as handovers from the weaker 2023-24 sales cohort worked through; gross margin ticked up to ~14.3%.
Announced H1 2026 attributable contracted sales of ~RMB48.87bn, down ~8.4% YoY, continuing the multi-period sales decline.

Citi reiterated a Buy rating, citing an accelerating land-acquisition pace and expectation of more new project launches from September 2026; Bank of America, CICC, Huatai and HSBC also maintained Buy/Outperform with targets in the HK$18-22 range (vs. shares trading near HK$15).

Morgan Stanley cut its price target to HK$19.30 from HK$21.18, still above the prevailing share price, while CICC cut its 2026/2027 profit forecasts by 18%/25% on lower expected settlement volumes but kept an Outperform rating and HK$22.3 target, citing state-backed funding support.
May 2026 equity contracted sales reportedly rose ~13% YoY, prompting some analysts (Morgan Stanley) to flag the company as likely to outperform peers near-term.

Scrip dividend conversion price for the FY2025 final dividend (HK$0.9/share) set at HK$15.16; shareholders had until 30 June 2026 to elect scrip, reflecting a continued policy of cash-conservation-friendly shareholder returns.
Board changes: Cheng Dongfang appointed non-executive director (24 April 2026); Zhao Chengmin resigned as executive director (7 August 2026); Ye Yanliu added to Nomination Committee.

FY2025 revenue RMB136.79bn (-4.3% YoY), profit attributable to equity holders RMB3.65bn (-24.0% YoY), gearing ratio improved slightly to 87.5% from 87.6%, net debt/equity rose to 34.81% from 31.78%; declared final dividend HK$0.9/share with scrip option.

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026) and H1 2026 Interim Report (September 2026)

items.metric: Strategic priorities (no formal numeric revenue/profit guidance issued)
items.target: Strengthen core property development business; accelerate cultivation of a 'second growth curve' (property management, construction management); deepen industry-chain synergy
items.notes: Management does not provide formal point-estimate revenue/EPS guidance, consistent with sector practice; commentary is qualitative, emphasizing prudent land acquisition aligned with the balance sheet and continued cost/expense discipline.

items.target: Prudent, selective acquisition focused on core/deep-cultivated cities, with investment intensity 'appropriately aligned' with asset-liability position
items.notes: FY2025 added 41 projects for ~RMB65.4bn acquisition cost / ~RMB130.4bn total project value; management signals continued but disciplined expansion, not aggressive scaling.

items.target: More new project launches expected from September 2026 (per Citi, based on management commentary on land-bank conversion)
items.notes: Analyst-sourced, tied to the pace of 2025-26 land acquisitions converting to saleable inventory.

items.target: Continue reducing blended borrowing cost (reported trending toward ~3.1-3.2%)
items.notes: Total borrowing cost fell from RMB3.0bn (FY2024) to RMB2.26bn (FY2025) on lower total borrowings and lower average rates; trend highlighted as a differentiator versus private-sector peers.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Lin Weiguo's FY2025 statement frames 2026 as a year to 'reignite entrepreneurial passion' and pursue disciplined growth: optimize existing inventory, reinforce new project increments, and deepen industry-chain synergy, while acknowledging the real estate market is 'expected to continue to face challenges in achieving stabilisation.' Management explicitly prioritizes cash-flow security over volume growth ('adhere to the principle of expenditure based on income').

bull_case: State-owned parent (C&D Inc. group) provides funding access, lower borrowing costs (~3.1-3.2% blended, among the lowest in the sector) and implicit support that most private developers lack, positioning C&D International as a consolidation winner as weaker peers exit or shrink

Recent, higher-quality land bank (83% acquired post-2022) reduces legacy impairment risk and should support margins and sell-through rates relative to developers still working through 2017-2021 vintage land

'Flagship project' strategy has demonstrably outsold local competing projects in core cities (Xiamen, Beijing, Shanghai), supporting premium pricing and brand differentiation in a market where most competitors are discounting

Analyst consensus is broadly positive (multiple Buy/Outperform ratings, targets in the HK$18-22 range vs. a mid-October 2026 share price near HK$15), with several brokers citing improving land-acquisition pace and cost of capital
'Second curve' businesses (C&D Property HK.02156, C&D Holsin SH.603909) are growing revenue double digits and diversify the earnings base away from pure development risk
bear_case: China's residential property downturn shows no clear bottom (Fitch projects a further 7-8% national sales value decline in 2026), and C&D's own contracted sales have declined in multiple consecutive periods (FY2025 attributable sales -12.0%; H1 2026 -8.4%), undermining the thesis that it can simply gain share into a shrinking pie

Revenue and profit are in clear decline as the weaker 2023-2024 sales cohort is recognized on handover - FY2025 revenue -4.3%, profit attributable to equity holders -24%; H1 2026 revenue fell nearly 48% YoY and profit attributable fell ~9.7%

Heavy reliance on parent-company loans (>50% of interest-bearing debt) for funding is a structural dependency, not a repeatable competitive advantage - if the SOE parent's own balance sheet comes under strain, or Beijing directs SOE deleveraging, this funding channel could tighten

Gearing remains high (87.5% total borrowings/equity) and net debt is rising even as cash balances fall, while declining margins (net margin ~2.7% in FY2025, down from ~6.6% in FY2021) leave little buffer against further price discounting

Large and growing non-controlling interests dilute the read-through from Group-level results to Company shareholder value, and the business carries no structural moat (network effects, switching costs, regulatory barriers) beyond state-affiliated funding access - a disadvantage that evaporates if sector-wide credit conditions normalize and private developers regain funding access
